title: From
hook: What is the town in From? Who are the monsters, what are the rules, and how has every season ended? A spoiler-full breakdown of From through Season 4 Episode 9 and the open questions the June 28, 2026 finale inherits.

sections.heading: The town you cannot leave: premise and rules
sections.body: From centres on a town somewhere in rural America that traps everyone who drives into it. Every road that leads out loops back to the town limits without warning. No map, no GPS signal, no compass bearing leads anywhere else. Residents come from all walks of life and all eras: some arrived decades ago and built a fragile community; others stepped off a vehicle yesterday and cannot believe what they are told. The town has no known name. The two main gathering points are Colony House, a Victorian mansion turned communal shelter for newer arrivals, and the residential streets where longer-term survivors live. Communication with the outside world is impossible. The surrounding forest has never been successfully navigated to an exit. By day the town is strange but survivable. At night something far worse begins. (Source: Wikipedia, From TV series.)

sections.heading: The creatures, the talismans, and the bottle trees
sections.body: After dark, humanoid creatures emerge from the forest. They can appear entirely human - smiling, speaking, mimicking friendliness - but they are not. They kill anyone they find outside and can tear through buildings by force, except for one hard rule: they cannot enter a home or shelter unless someone inside opens the door. This is the town's central survival mechanic. Residents protect their homes with talismans made from specific materials that create a barrier the creatures cannot cross when hung at entrances. A secondary line of defence is the bottle tree: a tree strung with the teeth of killed creatures, which deters further approach. Killing a creature is possible but difficult. In Season 4 Episode 9, a creature explains its view of the town's operating logic to a resident: 'This place is built on ritual, and with rituals, how you do something is just as important as what you do.' The community has mapped these rules through lethal experience over decades and passes them to every new arrival as a matter of immediate survival.

sections.heading: Victor, the children, and the boy in white
sections.body: Victor is the town's longest-known surviving resident. He arrived as a child and watched his family and an entire earlier community be massacred by the creatures, making him the direct link to whatever mechanism controls the town. Certain characters - including Tabitha Matthews and Jade Westin - experience visions involving a boy in white: a child figure who appears to guide, warn, or manipulate depending on interpretation. Sara Myers, a young woman, heard voices that directed her toward violent acts she did not fully understand. Jade, who has an engineering background, noticed symbols carved throughout the town and underground that predate any known inhabitant and appear to describe the town's rules in an undecoded language. An underground cave and chamber complex holds bones, markings, and evidence of far older occupation. The bottle tree at the entrance to that chamber is now central to Season 4's mythology: the boy in white told Victor explicitly that the bottle tree must not be taken down, a warning Victor treats as absolute and that puts him in direct conflict with Boyd's Season 4 plan.

sections.heading: How each season ended: Seasons 1 through 3
sections.body: Season 1 (2022) ended on two cliffhangers. A school bus arrived at the town limits carrying a new wave of trapped survivors, confirming the cycle of entrapment is ongoing. Tabitha Matthews, investigating a hole she found, descended into the underground tunnel system and glimpsed chambers covered in symbols before being cut off from view. Boyd Stevens, infected by a creature wound slowly transforming him, walked alone into the forest rather than risk others - and did not die, the first indication that some passage or protection may exist beyond the town's apparent perimeter. Season 2 (2023) followed the consequences: Boyd returned from the forest changed, carrying fragments of knowledge about what lies beyond; the Colony House and town communities fractured further over questions of survival and leadership; Jade's symbol research deepened into something that looked less like graffiti and more like deliberate architecture. The season closed confirming that the town's supernatural structure is not random - something designed it or something maintains it. Season 3 (2024) pushed further into the mythology. Victor's full account of the earlier massacre he survived was excavated, Tabitha's visions became more directional, and the boy in white's influence over events grew harder to dismiss. The season finale left the core group confronting the possibility that the town is a mechanism with a specific intended outcome rather than merely a trap - and set the Lake of Tears thread in motion for Season 4.

sections.heading: Season 4 through Episode 9: the Lake of Tears and what has changed
sections.body: Season 4 (2026) built around a thread seeded since the pilot: four words that appeared in cryptic form in Season 1, now pointing toward a location called the Lake of Tears. In Episode 9, Ethan tells Tabitha: 'We went to the settlement because Dad told me to find the Lake of Tears. Then bad things happened.' Whether the 'Dad' who gave that instruction was Jim Matthews or the creature called the man in the yellow suit - who can take the forms of people who have died in the town - is raised but not resolved. That creature has confirmed in Episode 9 to have killed Jim Matthews, and to have done so by entering a talisman-protected house in daylight: a direct violation of the rule that has governed the town's survival mechanics since Season 1. Elsewhere, Fatima is at the clinic with a heart rate of 19 beats per minute - medically impossible - and was given a brew by a creature impersonating a dead colonist named Sophia; what was in it is unknown at the episode's end. Boyd handcuffs Victor to stop him protecting the bottle tree and launches a tunnel operation: Tabitha and Jade descend into the underground chamber, believing a talisman's imagery identifies them as the two who must go. They pry a heavy stone slab off a burial site - and an unknown presence appears in the chamber: 'You know, you really shouldn't be doing that. Jade.' Episode 9 ends there.

sections.heading: Going into the Season 4 finale (June 28, 2026): what it inherits
sections.body: The Season 4 finale inherits an accumulated stack of open questions. What is under the stone slab Tabitha and Jade uncovered, and who or what appeared to stop them? What did the creature give Fatima and what will it do to her? If the man in the yellow suit entered a talisman-protected house in daylight, does the town's core survival mechanic still hold for anyone? What will happen to Boyd's operation with Victor restrained and the bottle tree down? Was the instruction to find the Lake of Tears genuinely from Jim Matthews or a manipulation by the creature? And at the architecture level: what is the town, who or what built it, what is the intended outcome of the ritual the creature described, and is permanent escape possible at all under any conditions? These are the questions the season built. The finale has not aired as of this article. No speculation about its answers is offered here.

final_image: Tabitha and Jade at the bottom of the underground chamber, crowbars in hand, the stone slab beginning to lift - and an unseen presence speaking Jade's name from somewhere in the dark.

lingering_questions.q: What is the town in From?
lingering_questions.a: The town's exact nature is the show's central unresolved mystery. It is a physical location in rural America but one that is supernaturally sealed: every exit road loops back and no one has found a way out. Through Season 4, the show suggests the town is a deliberate construct maintained by whatever force created the creatures and the symbols, but its origin and purpose have not been revealed.

lingering_questions.q: What are the monsters in From?
lingering_questions.a: The creatures appear human and emerge after dark. They cannot enter a building unless someone inside opens the door. They can take the form of people who have died in the town, a capability confirmed in Season 4. Their origin - whether they were once human, what transforms them, and what controls them - remains unresolved through Season 4 Episode 9.

lingering_questions.q: Who is the man in the yellow suit in From?
lingering_questions.a: The man in the yellow suit is the most powerful creature seen in the show. He differs from the standard night creatures in at least one confirmed way as of Season 4: he entered a talisman-protected home during daylight, breaking the rule that talismans keep creatures out. He is confirmed to have killed Jim Matthews. His identity and purpose are unresolved heading into the Season 4 finale.

No direct creative connection has been established. From shares thematic DNA with Lost - strangers trapped somewhere inexplicable, a mythology that rewards close attention, survival horror elements - but the shows are unrelated productions. From is created by John Griffin and produced by Midnight Radio for MGM+.

lingering_questions.q: What are the four words in From?
lingering_questions.a: Four words appeared in cryptic form in the Season 1 pilot. Season 4 connects them to a location called the Lake of Tears, which the central characters are seeking to find and understand. The full significance of the words and the location is being resolved in the Season 4 finale airing June 28, 2026.

lingering_questions.q: Who is the boy in white in From?
lingering_questions.a: The boy in white is a child figure who appears in visions experienced by multiple characters across all four seasons. In Season 4, he warned Victor explicitly that the bottle tree at the underground chamber entrance must not come down. His identity, allegiance, and whether he is guide or captor remain unresolved as of Season 4 Episode 9.

lingering_questions.q: When is the From Season 4 finale?
lingering_questions.a: The From Season 4 finale airs on June 28, 2026 on MGM+. Season 4 began on April 19, 2026 and runs for 10 episodes. The June 28 episode is the season's final instalment.
As of June 22, 2026, MGM+ had not publicly announced a Season 5 renewal for From. Season 4, currently airing, is the show's most recent confirmed season.
